evidence.quote: was glad they could not hear the persistent beating of his heart which gave the lie to his words.
do I look as though I thought there were the least chance of your killing me?

adjudications.reason: In the revision, 'gave the lie to his words' follows the shabby man's line and Tommy's silent hatred. No confident words of Tommy's come before it, and 'And why am I so confident?' answers nothing. Restoring Tommy's source line 'Do I look…', with a speaker tag, anchors both. Boris's outburst stays cut, so 'Don't get so excited' is omitted.

evidence.quote: “And if we refuse?” said the German quietly.
Tommy lay back on the couch.

adjudications.reason: With the couch beat removed, 'he said thoughtfully' directly follows 'said the German quietly'. That obscures Tommy's lever, the date. Restoring the source sentence fixes the referent and leaves the dependency line verbatim.

evidence.quote: His hasty action has given me the pleasure of seeing you all face to face.
“Dead men tell no tales,” said the German evenly.

adjudications.reason: In the revision, 'Dead men tell no tales' answers Conrad's excuse rather than Tommy's face-to-face taunt, which the source has it answer. The plan marks this run as optional. The smallest coherent repair is to cut the dangling threat and its reply rather than restore more banter. The German's 'Can you give us any reason…' then follows naturally on the Conrad exchange.

evidence.quote: The effect of his words was electrical.

adjudications.reason: This is a legitimate tradeoff. 'Slowly Tommy spoke', the broken-off '----' and 'The effect of his words was electrical' with the German's purple face still stage the climax. The plan does not require the pin-drop line.

evidence.quote: behind his casual manner he was racking his brains furiously.

adjudications.reason: Both layers survive across the whole chapter. Tommy's inner state is carried by 'racking his brains furiously', the 'pit of his stomach', 'Tommy hated him', the heartbeat lines and 'His heart was beating violently', set against his flippant banter. The thinning is an acceptable tradeoff.

remaining_concerns: Tommy now has two consecutive speeches with only narration between them (the 'Do I look' line and 'And why am I so confident?'). They read as continuous, but Boris's 'No… you do not' could be restored if space allows.
